question: How can I find out who owns a given land parcel in Spain: which register holds ownership, whether it is open, and the legal route and cost to obtain it?

answer.summary: Legal ownership is held by the Registro de la Propiedad (Colegio de Registradores, under the Ministerio de Justicia). It is not open data: a nota simple (9,02 EUR per finca online, plus VAT) names the registered titular if you state a legitimate interest; the registrar decides within 24 h. Catastro shows the fiscal 'titular catastral' only to the owner or authorised persons (free online); its open data has no owner. No bulk owner dataset was found.
main_caveats: Registro and Catastro can disagree: Catastro data are presumed true only 'sin perjuicio del Registro' (TRLCI art. 3.3). Land never inscribed has no registry entry; Catastro then names only a fiscal titular.

Price conflict: BOE-consolidated arancel (RD 1427/1989) sets 3,005061 EUR per nota simple; the Colegio charges 9,02 EUR online (doctrine DGRN). A 2026 draft RD would codify 9,02; not confirmed in force.
Registry information is for the requester's own use for the stated interest; the sede terms forbid redistribution or loading it into searchable databases.

Navarra (Registro de la Riqueza Territorial) and Araba, Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa run their own cadastres: the state Catastro certificate does not cover them and rules differ (Bizkaia: valor catastral not protected).
Public-notice route (BOE expropriation lists) gives owners only for parcels hit by a project, for the notice period, and with 'Desconocido' for some parcels.
answer.confidence_reason: Legal route, access rules and fees read on official pages and BOE; the actual nota simple order flow was not run (payment, SPA) and the 9,02 vs 3,01 price conflict is unresolved.

attributes.note: Registro de la Propiedad = legal title; Catastro = fiscal titular catastral (art. 3.3 TRLCI: Registro prevails). Navarra and Basque provinces have own cadastres.
Not open: registry needs interes legitimo; Catastro titular is protected data; open parcel data has no owner. Registradores open-data portal blocked to my client.
Nota simple/certificacion from any registrar; Catastro certificate by owner, authorised person, heir; BOE expropriation notices list owners; denial appealable to DGSJFP.
Nota simple 9,02 EUR online (BOE arancel says 3,01 in person); Catastro online free, Gerencia 17,97 EUR; Navarra cedula 6,20; Araba 3,44. Bizkaia/Gipuzkoa fees not found.
attributes.gap_note: Fees of Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa certificates and any post-2021 Navarra tariff change were not found on the pages opened.
